Ever wondered where a puddle goes after the rain?
That same water can travel up into the sky.
The water cycle takes it between ocean, air and land.
Sunlight warms the surface of rivers, lakes and oceans.
Some liquid water evaporates into invisible water vapour.
The vapour mixes with air and can rise with it.
Higher up, moist air can cool as it rises.
Water vapour condenses into tiny droplets around airborne particles.
Millions of droplets, or ice crystals, make a cloud visible.
Inside the cloud, droplets and ice crystals can grow.
Eventually they fall as rain, snow or hail.
We call all these forms of falling water precipitation.
On land, some water soaks into soil and rock.
Some flows downhill as runoff into streams and rivers.
Those rivers can carry the water back to the ocean.
Water can stay in oceans, ice or soil for ages.
Then sunlight can help it evaporate and begin another journey.
Look at the next puddle. Where might its water go?
